preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are between 1 and n (inclusive), where n is the first integer in the test case.

preconditions.expression: all(q[i] >= q[i-1] for i in range(1, len(q)))
preconditions.description: The array q is non-decreasing, as it is derived from a permutation's prefix maxima.
The length of q matches the given n for each test case.
The first element of q is at least 1 and at most n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= p_min[i] <= n for i in range(n)) and all(1 <= p_max[i] <= n for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Both the lexicographically minimal and maximal permutations p_min and p_max contain integers between 1 and n (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(p_min[i] <= q[i] for i in range(n)) and all(p_max[i] <= q[i] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Each element in p_min and p_max is less than or equal to the corresponding element in q, as q is the prefix maxima of p.

postconditions.expression: all(p_min[i] == q[i] or p_min[i] == p_min[i-1] for i in range(1, n)) and all(p_max[i] == q[i] or p_max[i] == p_max[i-1] for i in range(1, n))
postconditions.description: For both p_min and p_max, each element is either equal to the corresponding q element or equal to the previous element in the permutation, ensuring the prefix maxima property.

postconditions.expression: all(p_min[i] != p_min[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j) and all(p_max[i] != p_max[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j)
postconditions.description: Both p_min and p_max are permutations of numbers from 1 to n, containing each number exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(p_min[i] <= p_max[i] for i in range(n)) and any(p_min[i] < p_max[i] for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The lexicographically minimal permutation p_min is strictly less than the lexicographically maximal permutation p_max.

postconditions.expression: all(q[i] == max(p_min[:i+1]) for i in range(n)) and all(q[i] == max(p_max[:i+1]) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Both p_min and p_max produce the given q when the prefix maxima rule is applied.
